classification.difficultyReason: Identify the radius from each radicand, use the sign of the square root to choose the upper or lower half, and plot the intercepts; all four parts directly apply the semicircle form.

content.prompt: Draw the graphs of the following semi-circles.

answer.short: Upper semicircle with centre $(0,0)$ and radius $2$.
answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}y^2&=4-x^2\\x^2+y^2&=4\end{align*}$$
The positive square root gives $y\geq0$. Draw the upper semicircle through $(-2,0)$, $(0,2)$ and $(2,0)$.

answer.short: Lower semicircle with centre $(0,0)$ and radius $3$.
answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}y^2&=9-x^2\\x^2+y^2&=9\end{align*}$$
The negative square root gives $y\leq0$. Draw the lower semicircle through $(-3,0)$, $(0,-3)$ and $(3,0)$.

spec.sourceRegion: Question 6(b); keyed graph on answer PDF page 32
spec.description: Lower semicircle with three filled intercept points and no grid.

answer.short: Upper semicircle with centre $(0,0)$ and radius $\frac12$.
answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}y^2&=\frac14-x^2\\x^2+y^2&=\frac14\\r&=\sqrt{\frac14}=\frac12\end{align*}$$
Since $y\geq0$, draw the upper semicircle through $(-\frac12,0)$, $(0,\frac12)$ and $(\frac12,0)$.

answer.short: Upper semicircle with centre $(0,0)$ and radius $\frac43$.
answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}y^2&=\frac{16}{9}-x^2\\x^2+y^2&=\frac{16}{9}\\r&=\sqrt{\frac{16}{9}}=\frac43\end{align*}$$
Since $y\geq0$, draw the upper semicircle through $(-\frac43,0)$, $(0,\frac43)$ and $(\frac43,0)$.
